text:
Maria L: heads-up, my replay harness numbers look noisy when we run against the new kernel selector build. variance spikes at connection churn.
Jonah K: can you paste the harness flags? are you running HTTP/1.1 keepalive or h2?
Maria L: HTTP/1.1 with keepalive. harness uses ~1000 concurrent clients, each with a short session (3-6 requests). flags: --rps 800 --concurrency 1000 --keepalive=true --pool-size=0
Taylor R: pool-size=0 means every logical client is opening its own socket? that will stress ephemeral ports and TLS handshakes.
Maria L: yes, intentionally trying to mimic many short-lived mobile clients. but results differ massively vs our replay logs.
Li W: common pitfall: synthetic short sessions amplify Nagle + TLS handshake overhead. with HTTP/1.1 you pay one TLS handshake per socket life unless session resumption is happening.
Jonah K: also check TCP_NODELAY. many clients leave Nagle on, that adds latency for small writes. we historically set socket opts in our client lib to disable Nagle.
Maria L: confirmed we have NODELAY=false in harness by mistake. fixing now.
perf-bot: perf alert: build 2026.03-kerselect-7 shows +18% p50 tokens/sec regression on synthetic short-session workload.
Taylor R: that matches. Quick checklist: TLS session reuse, keepalive timeout, pool reuse, NODELAY, and HTTP/2 multiplexing. H2 removes the connection-per-session problem often.
Maria L: switched harness to NODELAY=true and retested: p50 improved ~9% but still noisy. variance down but means kernel selector interactions still exist.
Li W: what's the kernel selector metric distribution? are we flipping between int8/float kernels due to different seq-lens?
Maria L: profiler shows selector flip on identical requests when connection arrives from different source ports — weird. sample trace: 
```
selector: chosen=quantized_attn_v2
callsite: batch_size=1 seq_len=64
kernel_hint: use_matmul_fallback=true
cpu: 30% on worker 2
```
Jonah K: could be non-deterministic due to concurrency ordering when populating kernel cache. If two threads race to compile/choose, one wins and another uses fallback until cache warms. That explains initial jitter.
Taylor R: agree. We should add deterministic seeding for kernel cache keys in the runtime for reproducible kernel selection in tests. Also surface a "cache warmed" signal to the harness.
Maria L: added a tiny warmup phase (200 requests) before measurement and pinned client source ports to a small set to reduce churn. rerun shows steady p50 and kernel selection stabilized.
Ops-Jen: note for dedicated infra: if you run many short connections from ephemeral port space you can hit TIME_WAIT exhaustion on load generators, kernel starts dropping connections. we saw that in staging last week.
Li W: other quick tips for apples-to-apples: use same TLS stack (BoringSSL vs OpenSSL) on client and server; enable session tickets for resumption; prefer HTTP/2 or tune keepalive to be > test duration for long sessions; set TCP_NODELAY consistently.
Jonah K: for gRPC vs REST comparisons, remember gRPC assumes HTTP/2 multiplexing. comparing gRPC to REST over HTTP/1.1 with no pooling is apples-to-oranges. either run REST over h2 or force REST clients to reuse the same connection pattern.
Maria L: documented in the test README: added a section "client-side pitfalls" with the exact flags we used and a minimal repro script. snippet: 
```
# repro short-session noise
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -H "Connection: keep-alive" http://$SUT/api/generate &
  sleep 0.005
done
```
Taylor R: good. also collect tcpdump for a sample run and check for repeated TLS full-handshakes vs resumed ones: `tcpdump -w shortsession.pcap port 443` then `tshark -r shortsession.pcap -Y "ssl.handshake"`.
Li W: and if you want micro-profiling of TLS CPU cost: run `perf top -p <pid>`, sample for openssl functions, and compare CPU across runs with/without session reuse.
Maria L: thanks everyone. next steps: (1) push harness fix with NODELAY and warmup (2) add deterministic kernel-cache seeding in runtime (3) update docs and add pcap collection to our CI smoke.
Jonah K: I'll open an internal PR for deterministic seeding. tag me @Maria L on it.
perf-bot: note added to perf queue: investigate 2026.03-kerselect-7 regression.
Maria L: closing the loop — after fixes the regression is gone on replay harness, still keeping the short-session synthetic tests in CI to catch regressions. :thumbsup:
